mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions affecting corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening episode (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand indicators (HOUST) predict a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment deteriorates.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
regime_hint: labor market weakening coupled with weak demand
failure_condition: 20-day out-of-sample test shows no significant negative return when the interaction pattern recurs (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% suggests robust supply-side momentum that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with INDPRO expansion (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as expectations of future rate cuts improve equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically positive when CPIAUCSL remains above 3% for the subsequent month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for the first time in three months, a positive S&P 500 forward return is expected over the next 60 days as a labor market recovery signals accommodative monetary policy.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.0% after two consecutive months at or above 4.0%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no correlation with UNRATE crossing below 4% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above the prior month's level combined with a decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days due to conflicting labor and supply signals.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases sharply while RSAFS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction pattern recurs but 20-day returns remain non-negative (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in residential investment (assumed proxy via HOUST, though not ideal, as a fallback) above 1,500 suggests a supply-side acceleration that yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST continues rising (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the 10-year yield proxy (not available in the catalog; fallback: FEDFUNDS below 4% for 3 months) predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as investors anticipate further rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 4.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically negative during the identified regime (p > 0.05).
